text: Before publishing: a draft app can only be tested by you and your plan's admins.
quote: While in draft, you and admins for your plan can test your OAuth app.

text: Before approval: a private app only works for users in the team or org it belongs to.
quote: Private OAuth apps can be used to make requests on behalf of users in team or organization you associated your app with
fix: A private app only works for users in the team or org it belongs to, and it needs no Figma review.
note: Page says private apps don't require review by Figma, so 'Before approval' framing is wrong; the team/org restriction is permanent, not pre-approval.

text: The app must be associated with a team or organization; its users don't need to belong to it.
quote: The OAuth app must be associated with a team or organization. note Note: Users of your application don’t need to be a part of the team or organization you select.

text: Public apps need testing instructions and any trial access or login credentials the reviewer needs.
quote: If necessary for working with your application, provide a free trial URL or login credentials that the OAuth app reviewer can use to access your application.
note: Testing steps are also required: 'Enter all the steps that are required...'.

text: Apps need an accurate name, description and an icon that matches your brand.
quote: Your Figma Community App must include an accurate name and description, and an icon that matches your application’s brand.
note: Guidelines apply to Figma Community (public) apps.

text: Provide a support contact and keep it accurate.
quote: Please ensure that your contact information is accurate and complete for users in the event they have any questions, support issues, or feedback.
note: Also: 'Established a way for users to contact you for support.'

text: Apps must not bulk-export file content or index files through the projects endpoints.
quote: Figma Community Apps may not use the projects endpoints to enumerate the files in an organization/team.
note: Page also: 'Figma does not currently permit bulk export of Figma file content by Figma Community Apps.' Applies to public Community apps.

text: Users must authorize in a web browser; WebViews are not supported.
quote: the user must access the authentication URL using a web browser, not an embedded WebView inside your application. WebView access to the Figma OAuth flow is not supported.

text: The client secret is shown only once when you create the app.
quote: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret for your OAuth app and store them securely. This is the only opportunity you have to obtain the Client Secret.

text: Any change to a published public app needs another review.
quote: In the case of published public apps, changes to configuration will require your OAuth app to be re-reviewed.
note: Page says 'changes to configuration'; 'any change' is a close paraphrase.

text: files:read and file_read are deprecated; apps must use granular scopes.
quote: We're removing the deprecated files:read and file_read scopes.
note: Page says the scopes are being removed and apps must update to granular scopes.

text: Existing apps marked 'Update required' must be republished to meet the November 17, 2025 rules.
quote: The changes went into effect on November 17, 2025. If you haven't re-published your app yet, you'll need to do so to meet these requirements.
note: Page also: 'we're adding an Update required label to existing OAuth apps.'

text: Write scopes like teams:write and folders:write work only in private apps on Enterprise.
quote: teams:write Create teams. Available only to private OAuth apps in an Enterprise plan.
note: folders:write has the same wording.

text: file_variables:read and :write are Enterprise-only scopes.
quote: file_variables:read Read variables in files. Note: Enterprise plan only.
note: file_variables:write also marked Enterprise plan only.

text: Authorization codes expire after 30 seconds.
quote: Note: Authentication codes expire 30 seconds after being issued.

text: Access tokens last 90 days; refreshing invalidates the previous token because Figma keeps one per user per app.
quote: Figma only maintains one access token per app for a user, so when you refresh an access token, the previous access token stops working.
note: Page: 'By default, access tokens expire after 90 days.'

text: OAuth rate limits are tracked per user, per plan, per app.
quote: For OAuth apps, rate limits are tracked on a per-user, per-plan, per-app basis.

text: Users on View or Collab seats get up to 20 Tier 1 file requests a month, possibly fewer under load.
quote: For View and Collab seats, requests are limited up to the given amount. Depending on traffic and demand, the actual limit may be lower.
note: Table: Tier 1, View/Collab: Up to 20/month on all plans.

text: Figma review of a public OAuth app (testing instructions, reviewer access) | wait: not stated; Figma says it varies with volume
quote: Approval times vary depending on current volume and the team’s availability.
note: No specific wait time stated.

text: Before sharing: a new 3LO app is private, so only you can install and use it.
quote: When you create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app, it's private by default. This means that only you can install and use it.

text: Before approval: users installing an unapproved integration are warned it hasn't been reviewed by Atlassian.
quote: Users trying to install an unapproved OAuth 2.0 integration are warned that the app has not yet been reviewed by Atlassian.

text: Sharing doesn't list the app on the Marketplace; you must send the authorization URL to every user.
quote: You'll have to send the link to all the users you want to grant access to. Enabling sharing doesn't make your app available on the Atlassian Marketplace .

text: Create an 'OAuth 2.0 integration' in the developer console, configure OAuth 2.0 (3LO) and add Confluence API scopes under Permissions.
quote: In the Developer console, select the Create dropdown and choose OAuth 2.0 integration to create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app.
note: Page also: Authorization > OAuth 2.0 (3LO) > Configure; Permissions > Add API.

text: Turn on 'Enable sharing' under Distribution before anyone else can authorize the app.
quote: If you want to distribute your app to other users, you must enable sharing.
note: Steps: 'Select Distribution in the left menu. Enable sharing using the toggle switch'.

text: Apps that store personal data must report those account IDs to the Personal data reporting API.
quote: All apps storing personal data must report user personal data, using the Personal data reporting API .
note: Page: 'You must report each accountId'.

text: Report each stored account once per cycle period (7 days by default, or per the Cycle-Period header), and not more often.
quote: you should not send reports more frequently than the cycle period for each accountId .
note: Page: 'By default, the cycle period is 7 days' and the Cycle-Period header may override it.

text: Erase or refresh a user's data when the reporting API says so; 3LO apps call POST https://api.atlassian.com/app/report-accounts/.
quote: Report accounts for OAuth 2.0 authorization code grants (3LO) apps POST https://api.atlassian.com/app/report-accounts/
note: Page: 'You must erase or refresh the personal data for your apps accordingly.'

text: For Marketplace approval, give reviewers access to a test instance of your software.
quote: In order to test the integration we will need access to a test instance of your software so we can run through the set up and configuration.

text: Add offline_access to the scope to get a refresh token at all.
quote: To get a refresh token in your initial authorization flow, add offline_access to the scope parameter of the authorization URL.

text: Refresh tokens rotate; store the new one every time, since the old one is disabled.
quote: You receive a new refresh token as well and the refresh token you used for the request is disabled.

text: A refresh token expires after 90 days of inactivity, and then the user must re-authorize.
quote: Inactivity expiry time 90 days A rotating refresh token expires if the user is inactive for this period.
note: Page: 'Users need to initiate the entire authorization flow from the beginning to get a new refresh token.'

text: Changing scopes forces users who already consented to consent again.
quote: Note that users who previously consented to the scopes will need to re-consent to the new scopes.

text: API calls go to api.atlassian.com/ex/confluence/{cloudid}; get the cloudid from accessible-resources.
quote: https://api.atlassian.com/ex/confluence/{cloudid}/{api}
note: cloudid comes from GET /oauth/token/accessible-resources.

text: Site-scoped grants make users pick one site per consent, so multi-site installs mean repeating the flow.
quote: The consent screen currently requires the user to select the site where they want to install the app.
note: Page: 'the user would need to repeat the installation process multiple times.' Listed under Grant limitations.

text: Admins can't revoke one user's grant from Connected Apps; they can only uninstall the app.
quote: An admin can't revoke a user's access to an app through the Connected Apps user screen.
note: Page: 'An admin can only choose to uninstall the app to restrict a user's access.'

text: Without passing security review you can't list on AgentExchange or distribute your solution there.
quote: Not Approved: The security review team detected security issues in your solution. You can’t list your solution on AgentExchange or distribute it to customers.

text: A customer org admin may need to install or approve your app before users can connect.
quote: These errors usually mean Salesforce is blocking OAuth because the connected app has not been installed or approved for the org.
note: Fetched from Composio FAQ accordion (embedded page data).

text: Creating Connected Apps is restricted as of Spring '26; Salesforce recommends External Client Apps instead.
quote: Creating connected apps is restricted as of Spring ‘26. You can continue to use existing connected apps during and after Spring ‘26. However, we recommend using external client apps instead.
note: Page blocked to curl (403); read via Playwright.

text: Creating a Connected App now needs Salesforce Support to enable an org permission, once per org.
quote: If you need to create a connected app, Salesforce Customer Support must enable an org perm in your org. This is a one-time process per org.
note: Read via Playwright.

text: Security review requires ISV Partner Program enrollment, a Lightning Ready solution and a Partner Console provider profile.
quote: Enroll your solution in the ISV Partner Program. Certify that your solution is Lightning Ready .
note: Also: 'In the AgentExchange Partner Console, create a provider profile.' and connect your packaging org. Read via Playwright.

text: API-only submissions need a Developer Edition org, credentials for external components, DAST scan reports, false-positive notes if any, and solution documentation.
quote: URLs and login credentials for external components requiring authentication
note: Table API Only column: Developer Edition org, external-component credentials, DAST reports, false positives doc (if applicable), solution documentation. Read via Playwright.

text: Reviewers test external web apps and services your solution uses, following where Salesforce data goes.
quote: To determine testing scope, we typically use a follow-the-data approach. Wherever the customer goes, we go.
note: Page lists 'External web applications or services.'

text: OAUTH_APPROVAL_ERROR_GENERIC or 'app must be installed into org' means an org admin must approve or install the app.
quote: Ask a Salesforce org admin to approve or install the connected app.

text: Distributing an External Client App to other orgs is done through a second-generation managed package.
quote: perhaps the greatest advantage of using External Client Apps is the ability to distribute them with second-generation managed packages.
note: Page presents 2GP as the distribution method; doesn't say it's the only one.

text: OAuth consumer credentials are global settings that must stay in a long-lived org, not in the package.
quote: These settings must not be packaged but stored on a non-ephemeral org that exists throughout the life of all packages.

text: Refresh token expiry is set by the app's OAuth policy, so check it before going live.
quote: In the OAuth Policies section, for the Refresh Token Policy field, click Expire refresh token after: and enter 90 days or less.
note: Page is about a connected app for Salesforce CLI; it recommends 90 days or less as best practice.

text: Apps that skip pre-testing rarely pass review, and each resubmission adds 2-3 weeks.
quote: Applicants who don’t test beforehand rarely pass and must resubmit after addressing security vulnerabilities identified during a review.
fix: Apps that skip pre-testing rarely pass review, and re-testing a resubmission typically takes 2-3 weeks (an estimate).
note: The 2-3 weeks is the typical time for Product Security to test a resubmission and is labeled an estimate; 'adds' overstates it.

text: Security review fee for paid apps; no fee if you distribute for free (amount not on current docs page)
quote: Use the security review submission interface to share your solution and required materials and to pay the security review fee. If you plan to distribute your solution for free, you don’t pay the fee.
note: No fee amount on page.

text: Without privacy policy and terms of service URLs, other users cannot authorize the integration.
quote: must be provided before sharing your OAuth integration with other users - if you have not provided them, other users will not be able to authorize your integration.
note: JS-rendered; read via Playwright.

text: API limit is 5 requests per second per base; a 429 means waiting 30 seconds.
quote: The API is limited to 5 requests per second per base.
note: Page: 'you will receive a 429 status code and will need to wait 30 seconds'.

text: Keep token requests below 10 per second per token.
quote: Note: frequent invalid refresh requests may result in token revocation. Please keep requests below 10 per second per token.
fix: Keep refresh requests below 10 per second per token.
note: The limit appears in a note about refresh requests, not token requests in general.

text: Register at airtable.com/create/oauth with a unique name and a valid redirect URL.
quote: Give your integration a unique name and register a valid redirect URL and click ‘Register integration’.
note: Panel is at /create/oauth.

text: Redirect URIs must use HTTPS, except localhost.
quote: Redirect URIs must use the HTTPS scheme. Localhost URIs are an exception, and may use the HTTP scheme.

text: Privacy policy URL and terms of service URL are required before sharing.
quote: Privacy policy URL (required to share integration)
note: Terms of service URL also marked 'required to share integration'.

text: Generate a client secret if token requests come from a server.
quote: You should generate a client secret if you will be issuing token requests from a server.

text: Access tokens expire after 60 minutes.
quote: Access tokens expire after 60 minutes.

text: Refresh tokens are valid for 60 days; unused ones force re-authorization.
quote: Refresh tokens are valid for 60 days. If the refresh token is not used in this time, the authorization is effectively revoked - the user will need to re-authorize

text: Refreshing invalidates the previous access and refresh tokens.
quote: When a refresh token is exchanged for an access token, the previous access and refresh tokens are invalidated

text: The code exchange must happen within 10 minutes of the authorization request.
quote: This request must be made within 10 minutes of the authorization request.

text: Users choose which bases to grant and can change that at any time.
quote: These may change at any time (e.g. the user could add an additional base, or revoke access to one).

text: Frequent invalid refresh requests may get the token revoked.
quote: Note: frequent invalid refresh requests may result in token revocation.
